subject.title: fix(agents): prevent silent corruption when editing non-UTF-8 files

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally reject edits to existing invalid-UTF-8 files rather than retain the former apparent-success behavior that rewrites invalid bytes as replacement characters?
rationale: The code path is a deliberate compatibility change in core agent mutation tools; the supplied user report and runtime proof support fail-closed behavior, but repository policy reserves acceptance of this boundary for maintainer review and requires direct Codex-source confirmation.

options.title: Accept safe rejection
options.body: Merge the strict decoder after the direct Codex-source check confirms the cited contract, accepting clear errors for unsupported existing file encodings to prevent irreversible byte corruption.

options.title: Preserve old behavior
options.body: Do not merge this change and retain apparent success for invalid UTF-8 files, acknowledging that it can silently rewrite unrelated bytes.

recommendation.title: Accept safe rejection
recommendation.body: Merge the strict decoder after the direct Codex-source check confirms the cited contract, accepting clear errors for unsupported existing file encodings to prevent irreversible byte corruption.
